def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")
    validate = sub.add_parser("validate", help="Validate semantic closure registry and optional audit closure matrix.")
    validate.add_argument("--registry", default=str(DEFAULT_REGISTRY), help="Path to _semantic_closure_registry.jsonl.")
    validate.add_argument("--audit-dir", action="append", default=[], help="Audit directory to validate.")
    validate.add_argument("--require-closure-matrix", action="store_true", help="Fail if an audit dir lacks repair_closure_matrix.jsonl.")
    validate.add_argument("--require-effective-status", action="store_true", help="Fail if an audit dir lacks effective_status.json.")
    validate.add_argument(
        "--source-artifact",
        action="append",
        default=None,
        help="Audit JSONL artifact that must be covered by repair_closure_matrix.jsonl. Repeatable.",
    )
    validate.set_defaults(func=cmd_validate)
    effective = sub.add_parser("effective-status", help="List or write per-audit effective terminal status projections.")
    effective.add_argument("--registry", default=str(DEFAULT_REGISTRY), help="Path to _semantic_closure_registry.jsonl.")
    effective.add_argument("--audit-dir", action="append", default=[], help="Audit directory to summarize.")
    effective.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="Summarize every directory under Plans/.audits.")
    effective.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="Write effective_status.json in each selected audit dir.")
    effective.add_argument(
        "--source-artifact",
        action="append",
        default=None,
        help="Audit JSONL artifact to use for closure validation. Repeatable.",
    )
    effective.set_defaults(func=cmd_effective_status)
    refresh = sub.add_parser("refresh-hashes", help="Report stale owner/closure evidence hashes (--dry-run only; writing is disabled by DL-039).")
    refresh.add_argument("--registry", default=str(DEFAULT_REGISTRY), help="Path to _semantic_closure_registry.jsonl.")
    refresh.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Report updates without writing.")
    refresh.set_defaults(func=cmd_refresh_hashes)
    anchor = sub.add_parser("anchor", help="Print the content and sha256 that anchor.v1 refs cover.")
    anchor.add_argument("ref", nargs="+", help="Anchored ref, such as Plans/Planning_Ledger_System.md#unit=PLS-012.")
    anchor.add_argument("--root", default=None, help="Repository root to read; defaults to this checkout.")
    anchor.add_argument("--hash-only", action="store_true", help="Omit the anchored text.")
    anchor.set_defaults(func=cmd_anchor)
    append = sub.add_parser("reaudit-append", help="Append one re-audit row per reviewed re-audit record (append-only migration).")
    append.add_argument("--registry", default=str(DEFAULT_REGISTRY), help="Path to _semantic_closure_registry.jsonl.")
    append.add_argument("--records", required=True, help="Re-audit records JSONL under Plans/.audits/.")
    append.add_argument("--only", default="", help="Comma-separated closure_ids to append; default all.")
    append.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Report without writing.")
    append.set_defaults(func=cmd_reaudit_append)
    chain = sub.add_parser("chain", help="Show every registry row of one finding and what supersedes what.")
    chain.add_argument("closure", help="closure_id, finding_key or registry line number.")
    chain.add_argument("--registry", default=str(DEFAULT_REGISTRY), help="Path to _semantic_closure_registry.jsonl.")
    chain.set_defaults(func=cmd_chain)
    selftest = sub.add_parser("self-test", help="Fail-closed checks of anchor.v1 hashing and re-audit supersession.")
    selftest.set_defaults(func=cmd_self_test)

    if len(sys.argv) == 1:
        args = parser.parse_args(["validate"])
    else:
        args = parser.parse_args()
    if not hasattr(args, "func"):
        parser.print_help()

Every expected UCC-049..UCC-105 command has exactly one definition, in the owner unit this map routes it to, or is listed in contested.
Every outside_range_commands entry has exactly one definition in its explicit owner unit under all ordinary rules; no other out-of-range command joins scope (DL-471).
Every Markdown contract ref names a checked typed_contracts definition by unit/ContractName; bare unit refs fail, and discriminator branches match their named contracts and enclosing selector enum (DL-471).
row_groups equal the overlay's row-specific identity cells, and envelope equals the overlay's payload_required and payload_optional bullets.
Every non_definition_tokens entry quotes the canon that marks it, and every token a unit's compatibility or stale note marks is listed.
Every judgment a definition makes is in its judgments list with a key, a choice and a gap_note; no judgment claims provenance and no canon field records one; no definitions block holds a YAML comment, whatever it says (any # comment in the fence is a C11 finding), or a string that names review or evidence material (a C11 finding too) (DL-341).
No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, production build tasks, implementation files, or source code are created by this PlanUnit.
UCC-230 maps every active command row of the UCC-049 through UCC-105 strict schema overlay to the owner-doc PlanUnit that holds its typed payload definition (DL-333). A definition is one entry of a pm.command_payload_definitions.v1 block: a fenced yaml block whose only top-level key is command_payload_definitions, with no plan_unit_id key, placed directly after the fence of a command_contract PlanUnit in the owner doc that the owners routing below names, and that unit lists every command it defines in preserved_exact_tokens. A definition gives the command's UICommand.args, each field with a type from the closed vocabulary below, a required flag, a default and canon or gap provenance; its command_kind and response_kind; its owner request and its owner result carried by the CV-333 UICommandResponse; and error and disabled-reason codes narrowed from the overlay's closed sets by the error_narrowing rule. It never restates dispatch_id, command_id, source_surface or actor_ref and never changes the canonical type of a common optional field. The expected set is the overlay command_id rule over the concrete tokens of UCC-049 through UCC-105, plus prose_unit_resolution, minus non_definition_tokens, each of which quotes the canon that marks it. A contested command gets no definition until the coordinator rules. Owner disabled states that fall outside the closed set map to closed codes through owner_state_code_map and stay display detail; identity exemptions exist only where this map records them with a decision. The catalog stays the command-id and alias authority and its command rows hold no data shapes. Fields of type timestamp, url or path take no literal default: their default is none, their owners validate syntax at run time, and an owner that needs a literal default first adds its validation to the checker (DL-333 coordinator resolution 11). scripts/pm-command-payload-defs-check.py checks this map against the overlay and every definition against this map. Amended 2026-11-07 (DL-341): a definition records every judgment it makes in an optional judgments list; each entry has a key (command_kind, response_kind, disabled_reason_codes, error_codes, owner_request, owner_result, aliases for which alias tokens it records, omitted:<field> for a field it deliberately leaves out, or field:<arg path> for a judgment that is not that field's own gap_note, where a [] step names a list field), the choice the definition made, equal to its own value for a fixed key (for aliases the alias tokens it records, or none) and without repeats in a list, and a gap_note saying what canon lacks or where it disagrees. A judgment carries no provenance, and a canon field whose source or gap_note says JUDGMENT is a provenance finding. A definitions block holds no YAML comment: any # comment inside a pm.command_payload_definitions.v1 fence is a C11 provenance finding, whatever it says, because comments are invisible to tools and no word list can tell a recorded choice from a note. No string in a definitions block names review or evidence material (review rounds and findings, fix rounds and their reports, review files, the owner-answers folder, the evidence share, the Q5 design's sections or the fix reports' canon-conflict labels): canon text stands on canon, and only a unit fence's source_lineage cites evidence. A field marked nullable: true may be JSON null, with any required value, except a required row-group identity and a restated common optional field: neither the overlay nor this map records a nullable one, so both are refused. A definition may restate a common optional field, required or optional, only with its canonical type and with constraints that only narrow the inherited ones; this replaces the Q5 design rule that allowed a restatement only to make the field required or add constraints. Enum values keep canon's exact spelling: non-empty strings without surrounding whitespace, unique within the field. worktree_lifecycle_state is required when the command mutates worktree state, as the overlay cell says: the map lists the mutating commands and the domain_action commands that do not mutate (not_mutating), both lists always present, each command with canon evidence that names it, and a domain_action it lists in neither fails closed. identity_aliases records, per row group, a canon name that stands for an overlay identity name, with canon evidence, so gist_id stands for memory_item_id and investigation_id for debug_session_id and canon is never renamed. A conditional identity exemption keeps its field, requires it on every branch of branch_field except exempt_branch and forbids it on exempt_branch: cmd.runtime.approve and cmd.runtime.decline define both the node shape and the HITL-038 chat-tool shape, with blocked_sequence and allowed_action_id required on the node branch and forbidden on the chat_tool branch. Canon names only the chat_tool value of approval_kind; the node branch value is not canon, so the definition marks approval_kind a gap. A definition may list in owner_state_codes each owner state it shows as a disabled reason, with the closed code owner_state_code_map gives it, which must be one of its disabled_reason_codes. Owner states maintenance_cutoffs_pending (DL-403, DL-446, DL-447) and dedup_hold_pending (DL-444, DL-445) map to not_configured, and the thirteen CRAU-095 local-runtime reason codes map to the closed codes the map lists. Amended 2026-11-09 (DL-471): outside_range_commands is a closed list of additional concrete command ids, each with catalog_unit, owner_unit, the inherited row_group and a registration evidence line. Exactly one definition is required in that owner unit, under every ordinary field, identity, envelope, provenance, kind, result and closed-code rule. No namespace or other out-of-range token is admitted by that list. unresolved_tokens can record standing questions with evidence, a question_id, judgment and alternative. The two packet standings are decided by DL-471 Q-ID1/Q-ID2 and now appear in non_definition_tokens; unresolved_tokens is empty. A Markdown contract ref is typed only as Plans/<Doc>.md#<UNIT-ID>/<ContractName>, naming a contract in a pm.typed_contracts.v1 block directly after that schema_contract unit's fence in the same owner doc. A bare Plans/<Doc>.md#<UNIT-ID> is an error. The block has only typed_contracts at top level and no plan_unit_id key; its body has exactly format, owner_unit, vocabulary (this unit), and contracts. Each named contract is a nonempty fields record checked by this vocabulary's field/default/provenance rules, or a closed union with exactly discriminator, discriminator_source and branches, naming fields records in that same block. discriminator_source is required: in_record requires every branch to carry the named selector as a required const equal to its branch key; external requires every contract use site (including list items) to declare discriminator_source: {arg: <selector>} or discriminator_source: {owner: <record>.<selector>}. arg names an existing sibling selector enum; owner names the owner-held record and selector (create uses {arg: provider}, update uses {owner: stored_destination.provider}). Owner selection is revalidated against that immutable stored record. Source maps have exactly one key and nonempty identifier/path values ending in the selector; arg must match the discriminator name. Source maps on other types or in_record uses are refused. Branch keys are exact selector values. An enclosing enum selector must equal the union's branch keys. Named refs, including forward refs, resolve against the actual typed blocks, never merely a PlanUnit id. YAML merges, comments, duplicate keys, unknown block/contract keys, misplaced blocks and review/evidence references are refused as for command definitions. No other contract-ref form changes.

```yaml
plan_unit_id: F3-717
unit_type: command_contract
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/FinalGUISpec.md
canonical_text: >-
  Typed payload definitions (DL-333) for the fourteen notifications and sounds commands that UI_Command_Catalog
  UCC-103 registers and UCC-230 routes to this doc: destination create, update, delete, toggle and test,
  mapping update, runtime override set, and sound preview, upload, pack import, asset delete, asset restore,
  asset export and mapping set. Destination create/update payloads carry provider-specific profile fields from
  CV-298 for Slack, Discord, generic webhook, ntfy, Pushover and Telegram while storing only credential refs
  for secrets; destination test requires explicit user action, enabled destination authority, rate limiting,
  masking and receipt recording; sound preview is local only and must not send external notifications. The
  definitions block below gives each command its args, owner request and owner result in
  pm.command_payload_definitions.v1, with error and disabled-reason codes narrowed from the overlay's closed
  sets.
  Shared conventions of the definitions block: UCC-103 registers these ids in its fenced unit only and calls
  them "Domain commands"; no catalog command table or registration table states command_kind, args or
  disabled_reason_codes for them. CV-298 names the provider fields; CV-369 now types them through
  NotificationDestinationProfileV1 (DL-471), and the block does not restate them. Update's optional profile
  is a whole-profile replacement, never a field merge, validated against the stored immutable provider;
  absence leaves that profile unchanged. The provider cannot change through update: use a separately
  created destination and explicit routing changes. Both choices are decided by DL-471 Q-F2 and Q-F3. notification_destination_id and
  sound_asset_id are the UCC-101..UCC-105 row-group optional identity fields, made required where the
  command's subject is one destination or asset. No wiring row of these commands (Wiring_Matrix.production.json
  entries catalog.notifications_* and catalog.sound_*) names a request_schema_ref or result_schema_ref, so
  owner_request is none throughout.
gui_related: true

  - Destination create/update accept CV-298 fields typed by CV-369/NotificationDestinationProfileV1 without exposing raw URLs or tokens; update replaces the complete supplied profile against the stored immutable provider (decided by DL-471 Q-F2/Q-F3); test-send stays separate from local preview and never mutates alert state (UCC-103).

validation_surfaces:
  - python3 scripts/pm-command-payload-defs-check.py
  - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
risk_class: command_payload_shape_drift
```

dependency_anchors.text:
### UCC-049 through UCC-105 strict schema overlay and UCC-106 lineage exclusion

This overlay is the owner reference for every active command row from UCC-049 through UCC-105. It keeps the catalog as the command-ID SSOT while avoiding duplicated payload tables. Implementers MUST resolve each active row through the row range below, then through the row's concrete current `cmd.*` tokens or compatibility notes. UCC-106 does not inherit this command schema; its retained command-era tokens and current typed local actions have the closed disposition stated in the final row below. Amended 2026-11-05 (DL-333): typed payload definitions live in the owner docs that UCC-230 names; this overlay keeps the common fields and closed code sets and stays the command-id and alias authority.

Common fields for every covered row:

- `command_id`: every concrete current `cmd.*` token in the row's `preserved_exact_tokens`, except a token expressly marked retired, source-lineage-only, or non-alias in `compatibility_only_notes` or `stale_retired_dispositions`; grouped or wildcard tokens are family aliases and must normalize to a concrete active `cmd.*` row before dispatch.
- `payload_required`: `dispatch_id`, `command_id`, `source_surface`, `actor_ref`, and the row-specific identity listed below.
- `payload_optional`: `route_target?`, `OpenSubject?`, `project_id?`, `repo_id?`, `worktree_id?`, `run_id?`, `attempt_id?`, `node_id?`, `thread_id?`, `usage_event_ref?`, `usage_record_id?`, `provider_attempt_ref?`, `tool_call_id?`, `trace_ref?`, `receipt_ref?`, `receipt_refs[]?`, `raw_payload_ref?`, `query_session_id?`, `selection_ref?`, `confirmation_ref?`, `idempotency_key?`, and family-specific args defined by the owner-doc definition that UCC-230 names.
- `result_fields`: the shared closed v2 `UICommandResponse` schema in CV-333, consuming the separately owned typed result rather than duplicating its domain fields.
- `error_codes`: closed to `invalid_route`, `unknown_command`, `invalid_args`, `permission_denied`, `blocked_state_required`, `stale_projection`, `handler_unavailable`, and `internal_error`; family owners may narrow but not expand this set without a new owner-doc row.
- `disabled_reason_codes`: closed to `unsupported`, `not_configured`, `unauthorized`, `unreachable`, `degraded`, `partial_capability`, `blocked_state_required`, `stale_projection`, and `permission_required`.
- `owner_doc_ref`: the owner-doc definition unit that UCC-230 names for the command; no handler may invent unowned payload keys or fabricate `*.command_applied` events.

| Rows | Family owner reference | Row-specific required identity |
|---|---|---|
| `UCC-049` through `UCC-053` | Docker and Kubernetes command families: `Plans/Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md` CRAU-115; storage and capability details remain with `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md`, `Plans/Wiring_Matrix.md`, `Plans/storage-plan.md`, and `Plans/Tools.md` ContractRefs already carried by the rows. | `container_ref?`, `image_ref?`, `compose_project_ref?`, `kubernetes_context?`, `namespace?`, and `capability_snapshot_ref` for mutating or capability-gated actions. |
